q: Which recurrence describes the running time of binary search on n elements?
exp: One comparison, then recursion on one half.

q: Which statement about Prim's and Kruskal's algorithms is correct?
options: Prim's maintains a forest and Kruskal's grows a single tree
Both require edges to be sorted initially
Neither can handle graphs with equal edge weights
Prim's grows a single tree from a start vertex, while Kruskal's maintains a forest of trees
exp: Prim's always keeps one connected tree; Kruskal's merges components using union-find.

q: To prove that a problem X is NP-complete one must show that
options: X is in NP and a known NP-complete problem reduces to X in polynomial time
X is in P and X reduces to a known NP-complete problem
X reduces to a problem in P
X cannot be verified in polynomial time
exp: NP-completeness requires membership in NP plus NP-hardness via reduction from a known NP-complete problem.

q: Quick sort with Lomuto partition (pivot = last element) on an array of n equal elements takes time
exp: Every element satisfies ≤ pivot, so partitions are always of size n−1 and 0.

q: Single-source shortest paths in a weighted DAG (edges may be negative) can be computed in time
exp: Relax the outgoing edges of each vertex in topological order; each edge is relaxed once.

q: With coin denominations {1, 3, 4}, the minimum number of coins needed to make 6 is
exp: 3 + 3 uses two coins; the greedy choice 4 + 1 + 1 uses three.

q:
Match the algorithm with its design paradigm:
1. Huffman coding  2. Floyd–Warshall  3. N-Queens  4. Strassen multiplication
a. Dynamic programming  b. Backtracking  c. Greedy  d. Divide and conquer
exp: Huffman is greedy, Floyd–Warshall is DP, N-Queens uses backtracking, Strassen is divide and conquer.

q: The chromatic number of a cycle graph with 5 vertices (found by graph colouring) is
exp: An odd cycle cannot be 2-coloured, but three colours suffice.

q: For four cities with distances A-B 10, A-C 15, A-D 20, B-C 35, B-D 25, C-D 30, the minimum TSP tour cost is
exp: Tour A-B-D-C-A costs 10 + 25 + 30 + 15 = 80; the other tours cost 95.

q: In branch and bound, a live node is a node
options: that has been generated but whose children have not all been generated
that is a leaf giving a solution
that has been pruned by the bounding function
exp: Live nodes are the candidates still available for expansion.

q: The matching phase of the finite-automaton string matcher on a text of length n takes time
exp: One state transition per text character; preprocessing is the costly part.

q: Any comparison-based sorting algorithm needs, in the worst case, at least how many comparisons for n elements?
exp: The decision tree has at least n! leaves and so height at least log(n!) = Ω(n log n).

q: The 2-SAT problem (every clause has two literals) can be solved in
options: exponential time only, since it is NP-complete
polynomial (linear) time using strongly connected components
polynomial time only if P = NP
no algorithm, since it is undecidable
exp: 2-SAT is in P, using the implication graph and SCCs; 3-SAT is the NP-complete case.

q: The class NP consists of decision problems that
options: can be solved in polynomial time by a non-deterministic Turing machine
can be solved only in exponential time
are not solvable by any algorithm
can be solved using logarithmic space only
exp: Equivalently, a proposed solution can be verified in polynomial time.

q: The space required by the Floyd–Warshall algorithm (reusing a single matrix) for n vertices is
exp: One n × n distance matrix updated in place is sufficient.

q: The recurrence T(n) = T(n/3) + T(2n/3) + n has solution
exp: Each level of the recursion tree costs n and the depth is about log_(3/2) n.

q: Which pair of functions satisfies f(n) = o(g(n)) (little-o)?
options: f(n) = n, g(n) = n log n
exp: Only n/(n log n) → 0; the other pairs have ratio tending to a nonzero constant or infinity.

q: A topological ordering of a directed graph exists if and only if the graph
exp: A cycle makes it impossible to place all its vertices before their successors; every DAG has an order.

q: In 4-queens with queens already placed at (row 1, column 2), (row 2, column 4), (row 3, column 1), the column of the queen in row 4 that gives a solution is
exp: Columns 1, 2 and 4 are used; column 3 is not diagonal-attacked by any previous queen.

q: Assuming P ≠ NP, which statement must be true?
options: No NP-complete problem can be solved in polynomial time
Every problem in NP is in P
SAT can be solved in polynomial time
exp: If any NP-complete problem were in P, then P = NP.

q: Strassen's algorithm has the recurrence
exp: Seven half-size multiplications plus Θ(n²) additions.

q: The length of the longest common subsequence of AXYT and AYZX is
exp: AY and AX are common subsequences of length 2; no length-3 one exists.

q: In a depth first search of an undirected graph, every non-tree edge is
options: a back edge (it joins a vertex to one of its ancestors)
exp: An undirected graph has only tree edges and back edges in a DFS forest; cross edges cannot occur.

Which is the decision version of the travelling salesman problem?
options: What is the minimum cost tour?
Is there a tour of total cost at most K?
exp: NP problems are decision problems; the optimisation version is converted using a cost threshold K.

q: In KMP matching with pattern ababaca, a mismatch occurs at pattern index 5 (0-based). The next pattern index to compare is
exp: The prefix function value at index 4 is 3 (border 'aba').

q: Which algorithm can compute all-pairs shortest paths in a graph with negative edge weights but no negative cycles?
exp: Floyd–Warshall tolerates negative edges provided there is no negative cycle.

q: The recurrence for the optimal value of the 0/1 knapsack, K[i][w], for item i with weight wᵢ and value vᵢ when wᵢ ≤ w is
exp: Each item is either skipped or taken exactly once, so the taken case refers to row i−1.

q: Which statement about backtracking is NOT correct?
options: It uses feasibility or bounding tests to prune partial solutions
It always explores the complete state space tree before reporting a solution
It explores the state space tree in depth-first manner
It can be used to solve N-Queens and graph colouring
exp: Backtracking abandons a branch as soon as it cannot lead to a solution, and may stop at the first solution.

q: For T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n with T(1) = 1 and n = 16, how many levels (counting the root level and the leaf level) does the recursion tree have?
exp: Problem sizes 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 give 5 levels = log2 16 + 1.
